card.problem: Design the news feed for an Android app like Facebook
card.constraints: ["View list of Feed/Post", "Like count, comment count, tap on comment goes to detail screen", "Infinite scrolling list", "Type of content: text, image, video", "100 million daily users globally", "Creating posts, authentication and friends are out of scope", "Users must read cached posts, like posts and write comments offline"]
card.heard: Why cursor pagination rather than page numbers
card.say: A feed changes all the time. With page numbers, a new post at the top pushes everything down, so page two repeats posts the user already saw. A cursor marks the last post I received, so the next page starts right after it. It also stays fast at our scale, because the server doesn't count rows. The trade-off is that I can't jump to page ten, but a feed doesn't need that.

card.heard: How does a feed item get onto the screen?

card.heard: What if it keeps failing? Backoff, retry limits, final state.
card.say: I'd use exponential backoff with some random jitter, so many phones don't retry at the same moment. I'd cap the delay, for example at a few minutes. I'd also set a retry limit, like five attempts. After that, the like stays pending and the UI shows a small "not sent" mark with a tap to retry. I'd never show it as liked on the server when it isn't.

card.heard: 200 MB cache limit and logout
card.say: I'd enforce the 200 MB limit in the local store, not in the repository. The store already says LRU, so when a new post comes in and we're over the limit, we drop the least recently used posts first. On logout, I'd clear the whole local store, so the next user never sees the old posts. I'd also clear the in-memory store at the same time.

card.problem: Walk through the client architecture on the board
card.heard: walk me through the client architecture
card.say: Now the data flow. The ViewModel calls a use case, and the use case asks a repository. The repository decides where the data comes from: the network or the local data source.
